claim: A conserved forest nitrogen-cycle model is progressively extended with seasonal farm management and a multispecies food web, enabling management-scenario comparison before formulating sustainable-agriculture recommendations.

manuscript_evidence.supports: Forest total N conservation assumption; producer/consumer nitrogen, organic pool, inorganic soil pool, decomposition. Scene a is an aggregated mechanism.
Crop-weed competition, seasonal rates, sowing/harvest pulses, herbicide/insecticide application conditional on crops being present, and fertilizer input to soil.

caption: Overview of the nitrogen-based modeling framework. (a) The forest baseline couples trophic nitrogen transfer with decomposition under a conserved total nitrogen assumption. (b) Agricultural management introduces crop-weed competition, seasonality and external nitrogen inputs and harvest outputs. (c) A seven-node food web extends the model while retaining soil cycling and management. (d) Alternative management scenarios are simulated and (e) compared using nitrogen input-output efficiency, the study's nitrogen-turnover stability proxy and crop-weed sensitivity. (f) Model-informed farming guidance is distinguished from literature-supported extensions involving rhizobia/legumes and straw utilization. Diagrams are schematic; no measured or rerun simulation results are shown.
